text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovakia's major steel pipe producer Zeleziarne Podbrezova said it was now exporting some 40 percent of its production to European Union countries. The company said integration with the EU was crucial for its future activities.
- Interior Minister Gustav Krajci will be interrogated on August 6 by the Bratislava prosecutor for the alleged thwarting of referendums on NATO membership and direct presidential elections last May.

- The Association of Slovak Beer Producers demands the Czech beer Gambrinus produced in the Slovak brewery Zlaty Bazant be included in quotas on import of Czech beer. The agriculture ministry is expected to decide on the request by the end of September.
- The Slovak Antimonopoly Office investigated 118 cases of violation of competition rules and imposed fines worth 5.4 million crowns in the first half of this year.
- Slovakia will gradually increase energy prices to reach full price deregulation by the year 2005.
- Leader of the French far-right National Front, Jean-Marie Le Pen, is expected to visit Slovakia in September.

SME - French Foreign Ministry on Tuesday welcomed the Slovak Constitutional Court ruling that parliament violated Jozef Gaulieder's right when it voted to withdraw his mandate last December. The French ministry said such a ruling is in line with legal systems demanded for countries trying to become EU members.

- Opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) Jan Carnogursky said the opposition wants to call by the end of August an extraordinary session to demand the return of parliamentary mandate to Gaulieder.
- Slovakia's second largest shoe maker JAS Bardejov has laid off 2,000 employees, about half of its total workforce, due to failure to find markets for its production.
PRACA - The Confederation of Trade Unions (KOZ) has criticised the government for failing to implement budget cuts which, KOZ says, should be the main tool in battling the current economic problems.
- The state-owned energy monopoly, Slovenske Elektrarne (SE), said it was owe some 1.67 billion crowns in unpaid bills.
